Subject: Request: Multi-region failover SLA exception & on-call handoff

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this. We ran internal tabletop exercises this week and have two asks for Redwood before we can move forward with our multi-region deployment in EU+APAC:

1) We need a short-term carveout that relaxes the hard RTO guarantee for cross-region failover when APAC is involved (we understand the production RTO target is 15m; due to cold KV cache and DNS propagation we need to allow up to 45m for the first 48 hours after a failover).
2) Clear on-call handoff and escalation during cross-region activation — specifically a named on-call contact from Redwood who can coordinate cache warming and traffic routing during the window.

Could you send a proposed runbook and an outline of how long the exception would be limited to, plus any monitoring or roll-back conditions? Attached our FR/QA checklist and the FinPass SLA questions doc for reference.

Appreciate a response by EOD Wednesday if possible — legal will want this captured in the SOW amendment.

Best,
Maya
Head of Infrastructure, FinPass

Date: 2025-06-15T12:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Multi-region failover SLA exception & on-call handoff

Maya — thank you, and thanks for the checklist.

High level response: we can accommodate a temporary operational exception with guardrails. Draft proposal below (attaching a runnable runbook):

- Scope: EU primary, APAC warm standby. Exception applies only to cross-region failover where APAC is the standby.
- RTO/RPO carveout: Default RTO remains 15m for like-for-like failures; exception window up to 45m for the first 48 hours post-failover to allow KV cache rehydration and downstream service warm-up. RPO remains unchanged (best-effort replication).
- Duration: 90-day pilot maximum from the first activation date; automatic re-eval at 30/60/90 days.
- Monitoring/KPIs: token-level latency & token-processing backlog, cache hit-rate, DNS propagation time. Rollback if error-rate > 3% sustained for 10m.
- On-call coordination: during activation we will have a named Redwood engineering lead (we'll propose one below) and an escalation path to our SRE director. Tech contact will remain reachable via the thread and phone for the activation window.

Attachments: redwood_runbook_proposal_v1.md (proposed steps, pre-failover checks, cache-warming scripts).

Next steps I need from you: confirm you accept the 90-day max pilot and the rollback triggers; if yes I'll loop in Markus (commercial/legal) and Jonas/Karthik (SRE/runtime) to finalize operational details.

Sofia Ivanova
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Sofia — quick technical notes from runtime/SRE perspective:

1) Cause analysis: the majority of the extra time in cross-region activations comes from KV cache cold-start and model warmup (especially for larger sequence lengths and GPT-style models with per-shard KV). DNS changes are typically sub-2m if we use traffic-manager shortcuts, but cache warming can take 20–30m depending on traffic patterns.

2) Mitigations we can apply for the 90-day pilot:
   - Proactive KV snapshotting for FinPass at 00:00 UTC daily + immediate restore to warm standby when manifest updates occur.
   - Canary traffic seeding post-failover (10–15% traffic) to accelerate caches.
   - Priority batching for recovery traffic to speed token throughput for auth-heavy endpoints.

3) Measurement plan: we'll publish a metric dashboard for the activation window (cache_hit_rate, tokens_per_min, avg_token_latency, 95p RTO) and run a scheduled 1-hour failover drill in staging with FinPass pre-approval.

If legal/commercial are OK with a 90-day limit and the rollback triggers Sofia listed, ops can sign up to lead the activation and provide the named on-call for the event.

—Jonas
VP, SRE Ops
Redwood Inference
